SceneAct API (all coordinates in a world frame with Z up; angles in degrees):
from sceneact import *
Scene(name='Scene'), Asset(name='Asset'), Part(name, *nodes)
parent.include(name, node) attaches an asset/part while preserving its world position.
parent.members[name] retrieves a child; parent.remove(name) detaches it.
node.clone() returns an independent subtree. scene.replicate(name, new_name) duplicates an asset.
box(size=(x,y,z), center=(x,y,z), color=(r,g,b), opacity=1)
ball(radius, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
rod(radius, start=(x,y,z), end=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
rod(radius, length=h, center=(0,0,0), axis='+z', color=(1,1,1))
fillet_box(size=(x,y,z), radius=r, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1))
sweep_tube(points=[(x,y,z), ...], radius=.03, color=(1,1,1))
assemble(nodes, name='Assembly') groups shapes without merging their meshes.
fuse(*nodes), subtract(base,*cutters), overlap(*nodes), exclusive(left,right) construct solids.
node.move(offset), node.turn(axis, degrees, pivot=None), node.resize(factors, pivot=None)
modify a node and its descendants. node.turn(euler=(rx,ry,rz)) applies X, then Y, then Z.
Default rotation/scale pivot is the geometry's world-space bounding-box center.
shifted(node, offset), turned(node, axis, degrees, pivot=None, euler=None),
resized(node, factors, pivot=None) perform the same operations on independent copies.
node.paint(color, opacity=1) applies color to the subtree; node.rgba reads its finish.
node.centroid, node.dimensions, node.limits give AABB center, size, (minimum,maximum).
node.landmark('top'), node.landmark('front_left_bottom') return bounding-box anchors.
node.extreme(direction) returns a support point; projected_span(node,direction) returns bounds
along a unit direction; projected_width(node,direction) returns their difference.
snap(node, target, source_anchor='bottom', target_anchor='top', offset=(0,0,0)) returns a copy.
A target can also be a world point; then omit target_anchor.
abut(node, target, axis='+z', gap=0) places a copy after a target boundary.
center_on(node, target, axes=('x','y','z')) aligns selected center coordinates.
offset_at(node, reference, offsets) positions selected coordinates; None preserves a coordinate.
repeat_line(nodes, axis='+x', spacing=1) uses equal center spacing, keeping the first fixed.
pile(nodes, axis='+z', gap=0) spaces bounding surfaces, keeping the first fixed.
lattice(nodes, rows=None, columns=None, spacing=(1,1), plane='xy', center=(0,0,0), order='row-major')
orbit(nodes, radius, axis='+z', center=(0,0,0), start=0, sweep=360, orient=False, rotation_offset=0)
Layout functions return assemblies of independent copies.
scene.bind(source,target,source_anchor='bottom',target_anchor='top',offset=(0,0,0))
registers a persistent relation between scene members; scene.settle() updates dependencies.
realize(scene) settles constraints and creates Blender geometry, clearing Blender first.
set_view(position,target,lens=35,sensor=36,shift=(0,0)) creates the active camera.
area_emitter(position,power=500,size=5,target=(0,0,0),color=(1,1,1)) creates an area light.
Call realize before setting the camera and lighting. Estimate the input viewpoint yourself.

import bpy, math, random
from mathutils import Vector
from sceneact import *

random.seed(21)
scene = Scene("Historic tiled interior")

ivory=(.76,.76,.68)

for i,(x,y) in enumerate(((-3.0,-.67),(.90,-.37),(3.8,.66))):
    scene.include("barrier post "+str(i),rod(.024,start=(x,y,.03),end=(x,y,.86),color=(.39,.40,.36)))

def mat(name,color,rough=0.8,metal=0):
    m=bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    m.diffuse_color=(*color,1)
    m.use_nodes=True
    p=m.node_tree.nodes.get("Principled BSDF")
    p.inputs["Base Color"].default_value=(*color,1)
    p.inputs["Roughness"].default_value=rough
    p.inputs["Metallic"].default_value=metal
    return m

plaster=mat("uneven limewashed plaster",(.76,.78,.71))
p=plaster.node_tree.nodes.get("Principled BSDF")
noise=plaster.node_tree.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexNoise")
noise.inputs["Scale"].default_value=5
noise.inputs["Detail"].default_value=4
ramp=plaster.node_tree.nodes.new("ShaderNodeValToRGB")

ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].color=(.84,.85,.78,1)

bump.inputs["Distance"].default_value=.055

plaster.node_tree.links.new(bump.outputs[0],p.inputs["Normal"])

cream=mat("tile warm ivory",(.70,.70,.54),.5)
blue=mat("ceramic cobalt",(.095,.24,.31),.40)
teal=mat("ceramic turquoise",(.24,.40,.39),.45)
pale=mat("ceramic pale blue",(.47,.58,.54),.5)
gold=mat("old gold ochre",(.54,.39,.075),.48,.25)
black=mat("blackened cast iron",(.045,.052,.047),.67,.55)
darkwood=mat("aged brown oak",(.075,.047,.026),.85)

def mesh(name,verts,faces,material):
    me=bpy.data.meshes.new(name)
    me.from_pydata(verts,[],faces)
    me.update()
    ob=bpy.data.objects.new(name,me)
    bpy.context.collection.objects.link(ob)
    if material: ob.data.materials.append(material)
    return ob

def cube(name,loc,scale,material):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1,location=loc)
    ob=bpy.context.object
    ob.name=name
    ob.dimensions=scale
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(location=False,rotation=False,scale=True)
    ob.data.materials.append(material)
    return ob

def line(name,pts,radius,material):
    cu=bpy.data.curves.new(name,"CURVE")
    cu.dimensions="3D"
    cu.bevel_depth=radius
    cu.bevel_resolution=2
    sp=cu.splines.new("POLY")
    sp.points.add(len(pts)-1)
    for p,co in zip(sp.points,pts):
        p.co=(*co,1)
    ob=bpy.data.objects.new(name,cu)
    bpy.context.collection.objects.link(ob)
    ob.data.materials.append(material)
    return ob

def lathe(name,profile,center,material,n=48):
    verts=[]
    for z,r in profile:
        for j in range(n):
            a=2*math.pi*j/n
            verts.append((center[0]+r*math.cos(a),center[1]+r*math.sin(a),center[2]+z))
    faces=[]
    for i in range(len(profile)-1):
        for j in range(n):
            faces.append((i*n+j,i*n+(j+1)%n,(i+1)*n+(j+1)%n,(i+1)*n+j))
    ob=mesh(name,verts,faces,material)
    for poly in ob.data.polygons: poly.use_smooth=True
    return ob

# Four-sided taper of the broad extractor canopy.
verts=[
    (-.825,2.37,2.87),(.725,2.37,2.87),(.725,3.31,2.87),(-.825,3.31,2.87),
    (-.105,2.95,4.30),(.005,2.95,4.30),(.005,3.16,4.30),(-.105,3.16,4.30)]
mesh("tapered plaster smoke hood",verts,[(0,1,5,4),(1,2,6,5),(2,3,7,6),(3,0,4,7),(4,5,6,7)],white)

# The vault is an actual curved interior surface.
verts=[]; faces=[]
N=96; M=32

    zz=5.05+3.55*math.sin(phi)
    for j in range(N):

        verts.append((rr*math.cos(a),2.0+rr*math.sin(a),zz))
for i in range(M):
    for j in range(N):
        faces.append((i*N+j,i*N+(j+1)%N,(i+1)*N+(j+1)%N,(i+1)*N+j))
ob=mesh("high domed plaster ceiling",verts,faces,plaster)
for f in ob.data.polygons: f.use_smooth=True

# Broad arched plaster ribs, seen against the upper wall.
def ribbon(name,pts,width,material,y=3.08):
    v=[]
    for i,(x,z) in enumerate(pts):
        a=pts[max(0,i-1)]
        b=pts[min(len(pts)-1,i+1)]
        dx=b[0]-a[0]; dz=b[1]-a[1]
        d=math.hypot(dx,dz)
        nx=-dz/d; nz=dx/d
        v += [(x+nx*width/2,y,z+nz*width/2),(x-nx*width/2,y,z-nz*width/2)]
    return mesh(name,v,[(2*i,2*i+1,2*i+3,2*i+2) for i in range(len(pts)-1)],material)
pts=[]
for i in range(51):

    pts.append((-2.45+3.65*math.sin(a),3.63+2.26*math.cos(a)))
ribbon("left sweeping vault rib",pts,.16,white)

    for i in range(1,25):
        a=math.pi*i/24
        pts.append((cx+w/2*math.cos(a),y,z+h-w/2+w/2*math.sin(a)))
    return mesh(name,pts,[tuple(range(len(pts)))],material)
for i,(x,z,w,h) in enumerate(((-1.72,6.38,.43,.91),(.42,6.16,.48,.83),(2.58,6.60,.50,.91))):
    archpoly(x,3.13,z,w+.13,h+.08,mat("window reveal"+str(i),(.58,.61,.52)),"window reveal "+str(i))

def disk(x,z,rx,rz,idx,rot=0,n=10):

        tilepoly([(x-s*.49,z-s*.49),(x+s*.49,z-s*.49),(x+s*.49,z+s*.49),(x-s*.49,z+s*.49)],0)
        for k in range(8):

    mesh("top border blue diamond",[(x-.022,3.23,4.18),(x,3.23,4.235),(x+.022,3.23,4.18),(x,3.23,4.125)],[(0,1,2,3)],blue)

    for xx in (x-.29,x+.29):
        cube("door frame strip",(xx,3.08,1.16),(.045,.055,2.0),gold)
    for z in (.19,1.98):
        cube("horizontal door framing",(x,3.08,z),(.59,.05,.045),gold)
    # Small closely spaced gilded studs and fretwork.
    for row in range(14):

            ob.data.materials.clear()

area_emitter((-2.4,.6,6.8),power=1700,size=3.4,target=(-.9,2.4,2.6),color=(.91,.97,1.0))
